payload.question: This Apple ID security alert is visually perfect — it looks exactly like a real Apple email. How do you determine if it's real?
payload.image_alt: A near-perfect clone of an Apple ID security alert email
options: The email headers show it was sent via a third-party mail server, not Apple's infrastructure
The Apple logo resolution is slightly lower than normal
The email mentions a device you don't own
The support link goes to 'apple.com/support' which is correct
payload.anomaly_hint: This one requires checking behind what's visible — look at the raw email headers

explanation: When a phishing email perfectly clones visual design, the only reliable signal is the email's technical headers: 'Received-from', SPF/DKIM authentication results, and the actual sending mail server. In your email client, view 'Show Original' or 'View Source' — you'll see 'dkim=fail' or a non-Apple sending domain. Real Apple emails pass DKIM authentication from apple.com mail servers.
